claims.text: The alloy composition is equiatomic Nb25Ta25Ti25V25.
The initial alloy has a single-phase BCC structure with grains of 200–400 μm.
The 200–400 μm single-phase BCC state is the as-cast state.
The initial Nb-Ta-Ti-V alloy has limited ductility and low yield strength.
HPT at 6 GPa and 400–600°C for 1–2 turns will refine Nb25Ta25Ti25V25 to a grain size below 50 nm.
A subsequent low-temperature aging treatment will produce nanoscale coherent B2 precipitates in the HPT-processed Nb-Ta-Ti-V alloy.
The proposed B2 precipitates form through spinodal decomposition or nucleation during aging.
HPT refines grains through dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding.
Nanocrystalline grain refinement provides grain-boundary or Hall–Petch strengthening.
A CuMoTaWV RHEA film processed at 500°C had an average grain size of 18 nm and high hardness attributed to grain-boundary strengthening.
HPT-generated defects and stored energy drive B2 nucleation during aging.
The B2 precipitates are Nb-rich or Ti-rich and are thermodynamically favored over Laves phases in equiatomic Nb-Ta-Ti-V.
Coherent B2 interfaces impede dislocation motion while maintaining ductility.
The processed alloy will contain 5–10% B2 precipitates in a nanocrystalline BCC matrix.
The processed alloy will achieve yield strength above 1500 MPa and tensile ductility above 10%.
No brittle Laves phase will be detectable after the proposed HPT and aging route.
The as-cast alloy has a yield strength of approximately 500–800 MPa.
Aging above 700°C will cause brittle Laves-phase formation in Nb25Ta25Ti25V25.
HPT pressure below 4 GPa is insufficient to refine Nb25Ta25Ti25V25 below 50 nm.
Cr additions can induce Laves phases in HfMoTaTiZr and WVTaTi alloys, while annealing AlCoCrFeNi-related alloy chemistry can induce sigma phase.

contradictions.description: The boundary states categorically that aging above 700°C causes Laves formation in Nb-Ta-Ti-V, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that phase stability under deformation and aging is undocumented and that the Laves evidence comes from compositionally different Cr-containing systems.
